bib.title: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
bib.venue: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only. Figure 2b (memorization curves) has no numbers in the text, so none recorded.

question: Can a single-stage autoregressive transformer over EnCodec tokens, using codebook interleaving patterns, generate high-quality text- and melody-conditioned music without cascaded models?
hypothesis: Inexact parallel or delayed prediction of RVQ codebooks can approach the quality of full flattening at a fraction of the autoregressive steps.
contributions: A simple and efficient model to generate high quality music at 32 kHz, a single-stage LM with an efficient codebook interleaving strategy.
A single model for both text and melody-conditioned generation, coherent with the melody and faithful to the text.
Extensive objective and human evaluations on the key design choices.

method.summary: MusicGen is a decoder-only transformer with cross-attention to a T5 text encoding, trained over four-codebook EnCodec tokens at 50 Hz. Codebook interleaving patterns (delay, parallel, flattening, coarse first, partial variants) set how many autoregressive steps a clip takes. Melody conditioning uses a quantized chromagram; stereo is added by fine-tuning with 8 codebooks.

datasets.name: Licensed music training set
datasets.source: internal 10K high-quality tracks plus ShutterStock (25K) and Pond5 (365K) instrument-only tracks; licensed
datasets.preprocessing: 32 kHz, text description plus genre/BPM/tags metadata, downmixed to mono unless stated; 30-second random crops

datasets.name: MusicCaps
datasets.split: objective metrics on unbalanced set, qualitative samples from balanced set

datasets.name: In-domain held-out set
datasets.split: no artist overlap with train; ablations use 1K samples of 30 s; melody eval uses 1000 random files

models.name: MusicGen 300M
models.architecture: autoregressive transformer decoder, pre-norm, causal self-attention, cross-attention to conditioning, ReLU FFN D to 4D
models.context: inferred: 1500 autoregressive steps for 30 s with delay pattern

models.name: MusicGen stereo
models.tokenizer: EnCodec applied independently to left and right

other.finetune: 200K batches on stereo version of same dataset

other.note: retrained on the same dataset with the authors' open implementation
public API (instrument-only) for human study; FAD copied from original paper
FAD only, copied from original paper

training.objective: next-token prediction over interleaved EnCodec codebook tokens, conditioned on text (T5 encoder, cross-attention) and optionally melody
training.optimizer: AdamW, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95, gradient clipping 1.0; D-Adaptation step sizes for the 300M model only
training.dropout: text description dropout 0.5 after condition merging; word dropout 0.3
training.regularisation: EMA decay 0.99; condition-merging probability 0.25; condition dropped with probability 0.2 for classifier-free guidance
training.hardware: 32, 64, 96 GPUs for the 300M, 1.5B, 3.3B models; GPU type not stated

inference.max_tokens: inferred: 1500 steps for 30 s with delay pattern at 50 Hz
inference.samples: not stated per item; ablations use 1K samples of 30 s; human study uses 40 samples; at least 5 raters per sample
inference.prompting: text description; delay codebook pattern; melody as chromagram prefix

other.chromagram: window 2^14, hop 2^12, argmax per time step; Demucs removes drums and bass first

metrics.name: FADvgg
metrics.definition: Frechet Audio Distance with VGGish, official TensorFlow implementation

metrics.name: KL
metrics.definition: KL divergence of AudioSet classifier label probabilities between original and generated

metrics.name: CLAPscr
metrics.definition: CLAP score between track description and generated audio

metrics.name: OVL
metrics.definition: human overall quality, 1 to 100, MTurk with CrowdMOS filtering

metrics.name: chroma cosine similarity (SIM)
metrics.definition: average cosine similarity between frames at same time steps of quantized chroma of reference and generated

metrics.name: MEL
metrics.definition: human rating of melody match to reference, 1 to 100

eval.protocol: Mean and CI95. Samples normalised to -14 dB LUFS. Raters excluded if they did not listen fully or rated reference below 85. 40 instrument-only MusicCaps samples for MusicLM comparison. No seeds or repeated runs stated; FAD has no interval.

evidence.quote: we employ top-k sampling [Fan et al., 2018] with keeping the top 250 tokens and a temperature of 1.0
All ablations are performed using 1K samples of 30 seconds, randomly sampled from the held-out evaluation set.

results.claim: Flattening all four codebooks (6000 steps) gives the best FAD among interleaving patterns.
results.setup: 300M model, in-domain held-out set, 30-second sequences, T5 text conditioning

results.claim: The delay pattern reaches nearly the same FAD in 1500 steps.
results.note: Delay pattern needs K-1 extra steps in principle; Fig A.1 caption excludes the last step for simplicity.

results.claim: Predicting all four codebooks in parallel (1500 steps) degrades FAD sharply and lowers human overall quality.
results.setup: 300M model, in-domain held-out set, 30-second sequences; OVL 72.21 vs 79.69 for delay, REL 80.30 vs 79.67

results.claim: Other patterns: partial delay 1.51 (1500 steps), partial flattening 1.32 (3000), coarse first 1.98 (3000).
results.setup: 300M model, in-domain held-out set; value shown is coarse first (3000 steps)
results.table: Table 4, row Coarse first, column FADvgg
results.note: Partial delay 1.51, partial flattening 1.32 are in the same table.

results.claim: The authors conclude flattening improves generation but delay reaches similar performance at a fraction of the cost.
results.quote: While flattening improves generation, it comes at a high computational cost and similar performance can be reached for a fraction of this cost using a simple delay approach.

results.claim: MusicGen 3.3B scores highest human overall quality on MusicCaps against baselines.
results.setup: MusicCaps, text only, 3.3B model; MusicLM via public API
results.table: Table 1, row MUSICGEN w.o melody (3.3B), column OVL.

results.claim: Noise2Music has the best FAD on MusicCaps; MusicGen 300M text-only is 3.1, and FAD gets worse with model size on MusicCaps.
results.table: Table 1, row MUSICGEN w.o melody (300M), column FADvgg
results.note: Authors suspect noisy MusicCaps samples make FAD worsen once quality passes a threshold.

results.claim: Scaling the model improves perplexity monotonically, but human overall quality peaks at 1.5B.
results.setup: In-domain test set; 3.3B model; OVL 78.3 / 81.9 / 79.2 for 300M / 1.5B / 3.3B

results.claim: Chroma conditioning raises chroma similarity from 0.10 to 0.66.
results.n: 1000 files; 40 samples of 10 s for human MEL
results.setup: 1.5B model, in-domain test set, train Text+Chroma and test Text+Chroma
results.table: Table 2, row Text+Chroma / Text+Chroma, column SIM.

results.claim: Stereo partial delay is rated highest for overall quality.
results.table: Table 3, row Stereo Partial Delay (stereo), column OVL.

results.claim: DAC at 86 Hz costs 40% more inference runtime than EnCodec at 50 Hz for the same audio.
results.quote: thus reducing by 40% the inference runtime for producing the same audio
results.note: Stated as a claim, no timing table.

results.claim: D-Adaptation helped the 300M model but worsened 1.5B and 3.3B convergence.
results.quote: we observed improved convergence for the 300M parameter model, although for larger models, e.g. 1.5B and 3.3B, we observed the automated rule led to deteriorated performance

limits: Authors: no fine-grained control over adherence to conditioning beyond classifier-free guidance.
Authors: audio-conditioning data augmentation needs further research.
Training data skews western and Dance/EDM; oversampling other genres gave a worse model.
FAD on MusicCaps is not correlated with human ratings for the best models; authors suspect noisy MusicCaps samples.
Ablations are single runs with no seeds or FAD intervals stated; ablations use 300M only.
MusicLM and Noise2Music numbers are copied, not rerun; MusicLM human study used an instrument-only API model on 40 samples.
Training data is not released; learning rate value not stated.

terms.definition: A partition of (time step, codebook) pairs into sequence steps; all positions in one step are predicted in parallel conditional on earlier steps
Ps = {(s - k + 1, k) : k in 1..K, s - k >= 0}; codebook k is shifted by k-1 steps
